blogs.title: More Than a Scratch: Recognizing Capnocytophaga canimorsus
blogs.description: A deep dive into the clinical presentation of C. canimorsus, focusing on the classic 'dog bite' history, the hallmark pancytopenia and DIC, and the diagnostic challenges posed by its slow growth in culture. This post emphasizes the need for a high index of suspicion in the ED and ICU to initiate early broad-spectrum coverage.

blogs.title: DIC or TMA? When Sepsis Takes a Turn
blogs.description: Analyzing the diagnostic 'pivot' in this case: how to differentiate between sepsis-induced Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) and a superimposed Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA). We discuss the timing of laboratory shifts—such as the appearance of schistocytes and isolated hemolysis after the initial septic phase—to help clinicians recognize when a patient has transitioned from simple sepsis to a complex TMA.

blogs.title: The TMA Algorithm: TTP, STEC-HUS, and the 'Atypical' Rest
blogs.description: A practical guide to navigating the differential diagnosis of Thrombotic Microangiopathy. Using this case as a roadmap, we review the use of the PLASMIC score, the critical role of ADAMTS13 activity in ruling out TTP, the utility of Shiga-toxin PCR, and why normal C3/C4 levels do not rule out complement-mediated HUS.

blogs.title: The Eculizumab Tightrope: Complement Blockade in the Setting of Sepsis
blogs.description: Exploring the therapeutic dilemma of using C5 inhibitors like eculizumab in patients with active infections. We discuss the clinical paradox of treating complement-mediated damage while the body needs the complement system to fight encapsulated organisms (like Neisseria and Capnocytophaga), including strategies for timing therapy, vaccination, and antimicrobial prophylaxis.
